question: What does self-medication mean in everyday healthcare?

options.A: Taking drugs without a certified medical prescription
options.B: Buying medications only from licensed hospital pharmacies
options.C: Receiving free drug samples directly from pharmaceutical reps
options.D: Sharing prescribed drugs strictly among family members

explanation: Self-medication means using drugs independently without a professional diagnosis or prescription. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T4#GNS215_U4_T4_h1)

question: Why do many people in Nigeria turn to open-air drug markets for treatment?

options.A: Strict government laws forcing community pharmacy closures
options.B: Superior quality control found in roadside drug stores
options.C: Mandatory doctor referrals required for all herbal remedies
options.D: High cost and long waiting times in public hospitals

explanation: Financial constraints and delayed healthcare access push individuals toward cheaper, readily available informal drug vendors. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T4#GNS215_U4_T4_h1)

question: Which type of drug is most commonly abused through self-medication in local communities?
explanation: Pain medications like paracetamol and ibuprofen are easily accessible over the counter and widely misused for various aches. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T4#GNS215_U4_T4_h2)

question: What common practice leads to the widespread misuse of antimalarial drugs in Nigeria?

options.A: Treating any fever with antimalarials without diagnostic testing
options.C: Using antimalarials strictly as daily vitamin supplements
options.D: Injecting antimalarials intravenously at home without supervision

explanation: Assuming every fever is malaria without confirmation leads to unnecessary and incorrect use of antimalarial medications. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T4#GNS215_U4_T4_h2)

question: Which two vital organs are most easily damaged by excessive self-medication?
explanation: The liver and kidneys filter and process drugs, making them primary targets for damage during drug overdose or misuse. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T4#GNS215_U4_T4_h3)

question: A patient has severe right upper belly pain and yellow eyes after taking high doses of paracetamol for weeks. What is happening inside their body?

options.A: Pulmonary edema due to fluid retention in the lungs
options.B: Renal tubular obstruction from undissolved crystals
options.C: Acute hepatic necrosis from depleted liver glutathione
options.D: Gastric mucosal irritation causing internal bleeding

explanation: Too much paracetamol overwhelms the liver's cleaning pathways, destroying liver cells and causing organ failure. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T4#GNS215_U4_T4_h3)

question: What is the main cause of antimicrobial resistance when people practice self-medication?

options.A: Incomplete doses or premature cessation of treatment
options.B: Storing drugs in cool and dry environments
options.C: Taking medications strictly as prescribed by a physician
options.D: Using laboratory tests to confirm bacterial infections

explanation: Stopping medication early leaves the strongest germs alive to multiply and build resistance to the drug. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T4#GNS215_U4_T4_h4)

question: Why is widespread drug resistance a major public health problem?

options.A: Standard and affordable drugs stop working against common infections
options.B: Patients develop permanent immunity to all known diseases
options.C: Microorganisms become completely invisible under standard microscopes
options.D: Pharmaceutical companies stop manufacturing all liquid medications

explanation: Resistance forces healthcare systems to rely on costlier, harder-to-find backup drugs to treat basic infections. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T4#GNS215_U4_T4_h4)

question: How does self-medication delay the proper diagnosis of serious illnesses?

options.A: By temporarily suppressing symptoms and delaying professional care
options.B: By strengthening the immune system against future infections
options.C: By permanently curing the disease before a doctor sees the patient
options.D: By altering laboratory test results to show false negatives

explanation: Masking pain or fever tricks the patient into feeling better while a dangerous condition worsens inside. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T4#GNS215_U4_T4_h5)

question: A patient with ongoing lower belly pain takes strong pain relievers daily instead of seeing a nurse. What is the biggest danger of this habit?

options.A: Untiagnosed conditions like appendicitis may progress to rupture
options.B: Laboratory blood tests will become completely unnecessary
options.C: The patient will develop an immediate allergy to all antibiotics
options.D: The pain relievers will permanently cure the abdominal infection

explanation: Masking localized pain prevents quick medical checkups, allowing serious belly emergencies to become life-threatening. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T4#GNS215_U4_T4_h5)

question: What is an important first step for a nurse when checking a patient's medication habits?

options.A: Confiscating all personal belongings brought to the ward
options.B: Reporting the patient immediately to local law enforcement
options.C: Prescribing alternative herbal remedies for home use
options.D: Conducting a comprehensive medication history assessment

explanation: Asking detailed questions reveals hidden over-the-counter and traditional drug use that could affect treatment. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T4#GNS215_U4_T4_h6)

question: Why should nurses teach patients about the risks of buying drugs from roadside vendors?

options.A: To force patients to buy expensive brand-name drugs only
options.B: To ensure pharmaceutical companies increase their sales
options.C: To prevent adverse reactions and ensure medication safety
options.D: To eliminate the need for any future medical checkups

explanation: Patient education helps individuals make safe health choices and avoid fake or dangerous substances. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T4#GNS215_U4_T4_h6)
